name: Odeske-Holytsynske Subsea Gas Pipeline
monitor_reason: scope: field-to-field offshore line (gathering/infield), not a transmission pipeline. Sponsor, endpoints, length (83 km) and a concrete step (built, welded 20 Nov 2012) all pass, so a ruling on offshore interfield lines would move it to new_row.
researcher_notes: A Ukrinform story carried by Black Sea News says Chornomornaftogaz welded the final joint of an 83 km undersea gas pipeline on 20 November 2012. It links platform BK-1 of the Odeske gas field to platform MSP-4 of the Holytsynske gas condensate field. After commissioning, Odeske gas flows through it into the existing offshore pipeline and then to the onshore gas system of Crimea. A July 2012 Ukrainska Pravda news item reports the contract signed on 7 July 2012 with a planned length of 76 km; the 83 km figure is the as-built length. Both pages load and state the values, but they come from one company press service, so this is one source in effect. No existing row matches: the existing Ukraine roster has no offshore Black Sea line. Held as monitor because this is a short interfield link between two platforms, closer to field gathering than to transmission. Not staged as a row. If Baird rules that offshore interfield lines are in scope, the row would be Status operating, Fuel gas, Owner Chornomornaftogaz, Length 83 km, start Odeske BK-1 platform, end Holytsynske MSP-4 platform, Black Sea, in occupied Crimean waters which count as Ukraine under the naming conventions. Capacity, diameter and route were not researched. Chornomornaftogaz has been under Russian-installed control since 2014, so it would be noted as the builder in notes, not as the Ukrainian operator.
